summary: All 36 automated checks pass. Damage.assess and contactFace match my hand calculation for every case, and every hit goes through one code path in judge(). I found no play-breaking defect. Release is still blocked because AC-54 makes a release invalid unless the report carries measured per-class start/stop numbers and the speed-change figures split by cause. It carries only formula-derived expected values, and the Builder admits the harness lacks them. The Level 3 stall-breaker figures are reported, not fixed: 3/30 runs with an idle dummy and 10/30 runs with a wandering dummy, with a longest hold of 19.2 s.

walk_frame_rate_independent (203.2 vs 202.8 px) and run_speed_matches_spec. Class speeds match the spec.
deterministic_and_seeded passes. rnd is mulberry32 on state.rng.

lunge_distance_equal_8_directions (164.0 in all directions) and lunge_frame_rate_independent.
held_lunge_does_not_chain. step() computes a fresh press from prevLunge.
lunge_distance check covers the facing direction. By code, dummyStep uses the held direction if there is one and d.facing otherwise.
lunge_eases_out gives 87% at half time. ease3(0.5)=0.875, and its slope only decreases.
recovery_is_tweened: 0.35 s recovery, 19.6 px moved during it. dummyStep applies the easeOutQuad factor.
dummyStep clamps to the hall every step, including during a lunge. The solid-play checks also pass.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right, and drawEntry and placeCar by code. Top-left spawn paths start at 200 or more. See notes on Level 3 swerve.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right (14 cars in 60 s, no stall) and the traffic audit (L1 longest stop 0 s).

level2_cross_no_collisions, level3_free_for_all, solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play. axisMove truncates against every car.
No named give-way check. The carsStep yield loop matches car_to_car 2 to 5 on read-through: lower serials only, behind-exemption, follow target, decel/accel.
level3_free_for_all (4 directions, 6 classes). drawEntry draws the lateral coordinate in [200,520] or [200,800]. The 12-unit pool is covered by the spawn code, not by a named check.
Code: spawnStep stops at allocation and picks units from the first L.pool units. Allocation, quota and pool are in PARAMS.
write_off_card_and_fresh_body, ending_licensed. fc is edge-detected via prevConfirm.
level_progression, ending_decommissioned. levelEnd follows the spec's priority order.

rear_contact_pays_nothing. judge sets c.hit, records lastImpact and returns for a tail contact. Reach at full health is exactly 1.

Playtest. By code, drawRoads, the HUD level name, the cards, the perception overlay and the restart button are all present.

The longest hold of the lowest-serial car was 6 s with an idle dummy, but 19.2 s with a wandering dummy. The report does not say whether the dummy was inside the detection zone, so I cannot judge the 7 s limit. Report-only, per the CR.
levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic: all ended in 61 to 92 s. traffic_audit: L2 removed 0 cars inside the hall, longest stop 0 s.
No scripted breaker check. The stallStep code matches the rule.
Damage is two pure functions with no state reference. The only arithmetic outside Damage is sev = pay / maxPay in judge, which the spec requires for severity.
Hand-checked against contactFace: (31,0) is flank because a > ha is strict, (31.01,0) is nose, (-31,10) is flank, and the rear corners are tail. Rotation is handled by the dir projection.
damage_grid sedan: nose 635/1143/635/127, corner 381/686/381/76, flank 159/286/159/32, tail 0. These match the formula.

damage_module_is_logical, plus reasoning from the formula: the maximum lungeFactor is 1.8, the flank maximum is 0.45 of the nose maximum, and damage is monotone in speed and c. The full 5-degree sweep is not shown in the report.
damage_table gives 69 for the sedan bug case. By hand: 158.7*(1-0.8*0.7071)=68.9. damage_in_play_matches_module confirms the flank scoring in play.
By code: judge builds the contact, calls assess once, then records lastImpact and applies health and score from res.damage. The in-play check used a van, not the sedan.
judge uses the snapshot position, the pre-move car centre and outsidePoint. hit_during_any_lunge_step_counts_as_a_lunge covers head-on only. No check compares the faces at dt 1/60 and 1/120.
By code: assess returns 0 when speed is 0 or less, and a stopped-car contact still records lastImpact, sets c.hit and sets levelContact. The values 317 and 635 follow from the formula.

cruiseSpeed exists and speeds are clamped to [0, cruise]. vehicle_numbers_for_qa passes. The speed-step figures are not split by cause: 17 steps exceeded the 10 px/step down limit, with a maximum drop of 156. By code these can only be truncations, since every other change is slewed.
vehicle_audit.perClass holds expected values only (sedan 0.383 s up, 0.23 s and 15.9 px to stop). No measured per-class start/stop was reported.
laneDeviationNoDummy is 0 on all levels. Direction is never reassigned. Cars are removed only when wholly outside the hall, or by the breaker.
Outside Vehicles, only startLevel resets cars. judge writes only c.hit. Vehicles never writes dummy, score, health, mode or lastImpact. The only reduction of health is by res.damage.

Present: damage table, Lawrence case (69 and 1143), lane deviation, barrier clearances, breaker counts over 30 seeds. Missing: measured per-class start/stop and speed change per cause, which the Builder notes confirm. The gate is incomplete.
Playtest. The numbers support it: with-car diagonal flank 69, head-on 1143, standing 635, tail 0.

defects.problem: Per-class start/stop and speed-step figures are formula-derived or unattributed. Seventeen speed drops exceeded the decel limit, up to 156 px/s in one step, with no cause attached. AC-54 forbids release without these.

lastFx is not reset when the run restarts via confirm on the over card. The sim resets fxSeq to 0, so hit-stop and shake are suppressed for the first hits of the next run. Only the Restart button resets lastFx.

Level 3 has no lateral limit. A car on lane 520 or 800 can swerve up to 190 px, past the hall edge. A car on lane 200 can swerve into the x<200 or y<200 corner region. Cosmetic, and the Testpad had no limit.

damage_audit.comment: All values match my hand calculation. For every class, no result exceeds the head-on nose lunge. The with-car lunge pays 0.2 of standing on the same face. The tail pays 0. The bus nose head-on is capped at 2300, which writes off a fresh body as the spec allows. judge() is the only place that calls contactFace and assess, and it applies res.damage once to both score and health. Passive hits cost more than under CR-001 (635 vs 228 on a sedan nose). The spec acknowledges this.

vehicle_audit.paths: Cars never change direction. With no dummy, lane deviation is 0 on levels 1 to 3. Level 1 and 2 cars are clamped inside the barrier limits by limits() in latMove and swFeasible. Measured minimum barrier clearance with a wandering dummy is 9 px on L1 and 3 px on L2. Lateral moves need a free sweep, and an infeasible side means no lock. On level 3 a swerving car can leave the hall sideways and has no barrier.
vehicle_audit.stop_start: A car slows for these reasons: dummy conflict (brake-first classes and stuck cars), a lower-serial car whose sweep intersects (target 0, or follow speed), truncation against any car, caution derate, and an infeasible swerve (stuck). It restarts at accel 360 when the sweep test is clear or the blocker moves. Speed falls at no more than decel 600, except at truncation, which sets speed to the blocker's speed. Expected figures: sedan rest-to-cruise 0.383 s, cruise-to-stop 0.23 s over 15.9 px. Measured per-class values were not reported. The measured maximum speed rise is 6 px/step (exactly the accel limit). There were 17 steps over the 10 px/step down limit, up to 156 px/s, attributed by code to truncation only. A car can stop for good only through a chain of truncations, and the breaker catches that for the lowest-serial car.
vehicle_audit.removal: A car leaves in two ways. Normally it is removed when wholly past the far hall edge. Otherwise the stall breaker (stallStep) deletes higher-serial cars adjacent to or in the sweep of the lowest-serial car L after L has been held for 6 s. L is held with sees false. The breaker deletes without score. Measured: L1 and L2 removed 0 cars inside the hall in 3 runs each. L3 removed 4 cars in 3 runs of traffic_audit, with a longest stop of 19.4 s. Over 30 seeds of 60 s, the idle dummy had 3 cars removed in 3 runs, longest hold 6 s. The wandering dummy had 11 cars removed in 10 runs, longest hold 19.2 s.
concerns: Level 3 traffic jams often enough that the breaker deletes cars: 10 of 30 wandering runs (33%) and 3 of 30 idle runs (10%). The idle-dummy figure shows jams without any dummy involved. Deleting cars is a workaround, not a traffic fix. It is the separate change the CR describes.
The lowest-serial car never yields. If a higher-serial car is in its way, truncation drops it from cruise to the blocker's speed in one step, a visible jolt. The spec allows this.
The 19.2 s hold under a wandering dummy exceeds the stallLimit plus 1 s bound in AC-39, unless the dummy was in the detection zone. The report does not split the two cases.
The caution derate rescales the target speed, but the car still approaches it at decel or accel, so no instantaneous jump.

repair_requests.problem: AC-54 and AC-50/51 need measured values. The report has only expected figures, and 17 over-limit speed drops of up to 156 px/s have no cause attached.
repair_requests.required_change: Add a measured check per class: time from rest to cruise on a clear road (expect cruise/accel +/-0.1 s). Add time and distance from cruise to stop when held by a stopped lower-serial car, with gap >= 0 at the stop. Count per-step speed changes split by cause (truncation, caution rescale, other). Require 'other' to be 0 over the decel/accel limit. Re-run so QA can sign off.

repair_requests.problem: lastFx is not reset after a restart via the over card, so hit-stop and shake are skipped on the first hits of the new run.
repair_requests.required_change: When the sim restarts (mode over to attract), set lastFx = 0, for example by checking S.fxSeq < lastFx in the frame loop. Minor, not blocking.

notes: I rated the build as no regression against the Testpad. signature() now reaches 'wrong_face', which the Testpad could not. That is an improvement and not a scope problem.
The in-play damage check used a van at 100 and 110 px/s. A direct in-play sedan head-on check (expect 1143) would give a cleaner AC-47 record.
The lunge velocity direction is taken after the hall clamp. Against a wall the direction can degrade, and a zero velocity gives lungeFactor 1. This matches the spec.
The Builder's hit-stop restoration is render-only and does not affect determinism.
Releasing once the QA harness reports the measured figures looks likely, since I found no formula or code-path defect.
